children: An NBC News helicopter crashed in a Los Angeles neighborhood, killing at least three people while covering a deadly collision involving a Metro bus.
The aircraft came down in a parking lot near a self-storage facility in Chatsworth, a community in Los Angeles's San Fernando Valley, according to the Los Angeles Fire Department.
The helicopter was operated by Angel City Air and was providing coverage for NBC Los Angeles and its Spanish-language sister station, Telemundo 52.
NBCLA later confirmed that the two occupants of the helicopter who died were reporter Eliana Moreno and pilot George Marciniw. A third person on the ground was also killed.
News Chopper 4 crashed shortly before 7 p.m. local time Tuesday in Chatsworth, roughly 25 miles northwest of downtown Los Angeles, according to NBCLA anchor  Colleen Williams.

"We are deeply saddened to share that a helicopter providing aerial news coverage for NBC4 and Telemundo 52 was involved in a fatal accident in Los Angeles on Tuesday evening," NBCLA said in a statement. "We extend our heartfelt condolences to the families, friends and colleagues of those who lost their lives."

The bus crash, which involved an SUV and left at least two people dead and several others injured, happened just after 5 p.m. The helicopter came down between two commercial buildings at a storage facility and landed on two shipping containers and several vehicles parked in the area, the fire department said. It was one of a number of aircraft covering the bus crash.
The National Transportation Safety Board and the Federal Aviation Administration are set to investigate the incident.

Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass, speaking near the crash site Tuesday evening, described the events as a devastating loss for the city. She thanked emergency crews for their response and offered condolences to the relatives and friends of those who died in both the bus collision and helicopter crash.
Bass said five Los Angeles residents had died in the two incidents and said her thoughts were with those mourning their deaths.

California Gov. Gavin Newsom also expressed sympathy for the victims and their families, while thanking emergency personnel for their work. In a post on X, he said his thoughts were with those affected by the two crashes in Chatsworth, as well as the NBC4 community.
